articles.title: On the cusp of 24/7 service, robotaxis face pleas and protest in San Francisco
articles.summary: Waymo and Cruise are poised to expand robotaxi service in San Francisco to 24/7 operation. But city officials are concerned about blocked traffic, and some residents are using orange cones in protest.
articles.body: On a recent Friday evening, a driverless car pulled up alongside an outdoor dining shed in the Mission district of San Francisco, put on its hazard lights, and waited. As traffic began to pile up behind the vehicle, a man smoking a cigarette outside a nearby bar rolled his eyes. “I don’t drive a car,” he grumbled, “so I don’t really care about these things.” Other residents of this hilly city by the bay are not so ambivalent about the coming onslaught of autonomous cars. The California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) is poised to vote this Thursday on whether to allow Cruise and Waymo, the two main companies with autonomous vehicles in San Francisco, to expand their paid ridehailing services to operate 24/7. Currently, the companies only offer limited service. A vote in favor of the companies would essentially give robotaxis full access to the peninsula and its residents. They would be able to operate similarly to Uber or Lyft — travel anywhere in the city, at any time of day, and charge money for the rides. The vote also represents “the most significant regulatory moment for autonomous vehicles in the US over the last/next 3 years,” said Reilly Brennan, general partner at venture capital firm Trucks. [Image: According to Brennan, a robotaxi’s service area is also its total addressable market, a term in corporate finance that usually describes how much possible revenue a company can make. “If CPUC says it cannot operate 24 hours per day, you effectively have a reduced total addressable market,” he said in an email. “That’s why this upcoming vote is so critical: we’ll find out if the most significant US state (by revenue) is giving a green, yellow or red light to AV robotaxi’s future.” City officials are praying for a red light, or at least a yellow one. For months, they have been pleading with the state to delay the vote, citing a spate of incidents in which autonomous vehicles have stopped traffic, blocked buses, or obstructed emergency vehicles. The city’s transit agency and fire and police department have all logged complaints with the CPUC, calling for the commission to reconsider the plan for 24/7 service. “They’re not ready for prime time,” San Francisco Fire Chief Jeanine Nicholson told the Los Angeles Times recently. The department has logged 66 incidents since May 2022 in which robotaxis have interfered with firetrucks, according to The Washington Post. Many incidents have gone viral: robotaxis blocking intersections, forcing bus passengers to get out and walk, driving over fire hoses. In May, body camera footage captured a cop wielding a road flare at a Cruise vehicle, barking at it to “stay” as if it were an unruly puppy. After a mass shooting in June that wounded nine people, a robotaxi blocked a lane of traffic in the Mission district, slowing down emergency vehicles. The state’s Department of Motor Vehicles has logged nearly 75 collisions involving autonomous vehicles this year, including one last May in which a Waymo vehicle ran over and killed a small dog. The vehicle was operating with a safety driver in the front seat. The companies have defended themselves, noting that they are in communication with city officials about ways to improve to avoid future incidents. They also note that no one has been seriously hurt or killed by an autonomous vehicle in San Francisco, while many people are killed every year by human-driven ones. Pedestrian deaths in the city, much like in the rest of the country, have ticked up each year. There were 20 pedestrians killed by drivers in 2017 and 39 in 2022, according to city data. But some residents aren’t taking the slow advance of robotaxi coverage lying down. An activist group calling itself Safe Street Rebel put out a call on social media for people to place orange traffic cones on the hoods of any robotaxi seen wandering the streets of San Francisco, which would effectively disable it. “Cruise & Waymo promise they’ll reduce traffic & collisions, but we know that’s not true,” the pseudonymous account wrote on Twitter last week. “They block busses & emergency vehicles, create more traffic, and are a surveillance nightmare.” [Media: Autonomous vehicles usually have more cameras on them than typical passenger vehicles. Police could request footage from those cameras to investigate crimes or to violate residents’ privacy, advocates say. Waymo has received some requests for camera footage from law enforcement agencies but says it generally requires a warrant or court order. The companies were quick to condemn the orange cone protest, with a Waymo spokesperson calling it “vandalism.” An unnamed Safe Street Rebel told us in a Twitter direct message that some of the AV companies have “threatened to call the cops on us.” And the San Francisco transit agency spoke out against “ANY actions that may increase the number of disabled AVs on San Francisco streets.” The spread of robotaxis is testing San Francisco’s desire to continue to play guinea pig to Silicon Valley’s futuristic experiments. “I do believe people are both fed up with heavily distracted human-piloted vehicles / driver distractions *and* also that there has been a public backlash against AV fleets in some cities,” Brennan said. “There is a public chorus for a better, safer experience in cities.” Update July 11 9:40AM ET: Updated to include reactions to the orange cone protest.

articles.title: A 14-year-old is charged in fire that destroyed a driverless Waymo vehicle
articles.summary: The San Francisco Police Department Arson Task Force investigated, identified, and obtained a search warrant on a 14-year-old male for burning a self-driving Waymo taxi.
articles.body: The San Francisco Police Department has identified and served a search warrant on a teenager who is suspected of starting a fire in a Waymo self-driving taxi vehicle earlier this year. On March 27th, investigators entered the suspect’s residence and seized evidence that connects the 14-year-old male with the February incident in which a crowd destroyed the driverless car. The investigation was conducted by the SFPD Arson Task Force, which identified the suspect and developed probable cause for the search warrant. The district attorney’s office has filed charges against the minor while the juvenile probation department is deciding whether to put the suspect in custody before a court hearing. The February 10th fire was reportedly caused by lit fireworks that were tossed inside the vehicle as it was surrounded by a crowd in Chinatown. Involved suspects were seen smashing windows and other parts with skateboards before leaving a fiery carcass for firefighters to put out. In the past year, San Francisco residents have dealt with self-driving taxi annoyances, including blocked roadways and a Cruise car crashing into a fire truck. California’s DMV had suspended operations for Waymo’s rival Cruise in October after one of the company’s vehicles struck and dragged a pedestrian who was initially struck by a human driver. A Waymo car also hit a bicyclist earlier this year. Correction April 22nd, 2024, 12:57AM ET: A previous version of this article incorrectly identified the vehicle that crashed into a fire truck. It was not a Waymo vehicle, in fact it was a Cruise vehicle. We regret the error.

articles.title: Insta360’s GoPro competitor now has a bigger screen and improved 8K capabilities
articles.summary: Insta360’s new Ace Pro 2 features a larger, brighter screen, 8K video recording capabilities, and is powered by a pair of chips, improving its low-light recording capabilities.
articles.body: Insta360 has announced its new Ace Pro 2 action camera, an upgraded version of its GoPro Hero-series competitor. The compact camera now has a larger screen on the back that flips up 180 degrees for framing selfie videos, and it debuts at $399.99 — $50 cheaper than Insta360’s original Ace Pro. The design of the Ace Pro 2 still closely resembles the GoPro Hero series and DJI’s Osmo Action line, with an offset lens making room for an additional screen on the front. But while the front screen on the cameras of Insta360’s competitors can display full-color video, the Ace Pro 2’s monochromatic front screen only displays information. [Image: The front screen on the Ace Pro 2 is still limited to showing information, not video. That’s why the company is carrying forward the hinged screen from the original Ace Pro and has bumped its size from 2.42 inches to 2.5 inches (matching the screen size of the recently announced Osmo Action 5 Pro), while also improving its brightness and pixel density. A larger screen makes it easier to frame shots, whether you’re standing in front of or behind the camera. However, that hinge is also a durability risk depending on what you’re using the Ace Pro 2 for. The other feature that distinguishes Insta360’s new action cam from the competition is its 8K capabilities. The Ace Pro 2 can now record 8K video at 30fps — a slight bump from 8K at 24fps previously — using what Insta360 describes as a “next-gen” version of the 1/1.3-inch image sensor from the original Ace Pro that’s paired with a 157-degree wide-angle Leica Summarit lens. Still photography is also boosted to 50MP. Dropping the camera’s resolution down to 4K boosts frame rates to 120fps, or 60fps in HDR, while 1080p mode can record as high as 240fps for smooth slow-motion captures. Insta360 says the Ace Pro 2 is powered by a Pro Imaging Chip, handling “image processing and noise reduction,” as well as an AI chip running a “complex, custom-trained AI neural network,” powering a PureVideo recording mode. When recording at night or in places where the lighting is dim, the PureVideo mode can boost the brightness of a video while also enhancing details. The camera can also leverage its AI capabilities to automatically create edited clips featuring what it decides are the best moments in a video. [Image: An optional Dive Case accessory lets the Ace Pro 2 be used at depths of 197 feet. The Ace Pro 2’s waterproofing has been extended to 39 feet — six feet deeper than the original — or 197 feet when used with an optional Dive Case accessory. Insta360 has also added a new “wind guard” to the front of the camera to improve the quality of audio captured during high-speed activities but with a magnetic mount so it can be easily removed when recording in quieter situations. Other features include a larger 1,800mAh battery that Insta360 says is rated at 180 minutes but with video recording limited to 1080p at 24fps. In 8K mode, battery life will definitely be shorter than that. The Ace Pro 2 can also continually capture up to 120 seconds before a recording is started to reduce the chances of missing a shot, allows recordings to be paused without creating a new video file, and supports both hand gestures and voice commands for operating the camera from afar. What Insta360 didn’t announce today is an updated version of the Ace camera that debuted alongside the original Ace Pro. Its video capabilities were limited to 6K at 30fps, but it was $70 cheaper than the Pro. Had a new version of the Ace debuted with the same $50 price cut as the new Ace Pro 2, it would have potentially been a cheaper alternative to both the $349 Osmo Action 5 Pro and $399 GoPro Hero 13 Black while offering better video capture capabilities.

articles.title: Amazon’s online car ‘dealership’ with Hyundai is now live
articles.summary: Amazon is now selling vehicles through its website for the first time. The company has a deal with Hyundai to feature dealer models in 48 cities in the US.
articles.body: Today, for the first time, you can buy a car — yes, a whole car — on Amazon. Same-day delivery not guaranteed. The e-commerce giant’s first foray into car shopping is called Amazon Auto. The company is partnering with Hyundai dealers in 48 cities in the US to list vehicles on the site. Customers can browse, order, find financing, and arrange delivery — all within the familiar confines of Amazon’s online ecosystem. Of course, if you’re looking for anything other than a Hyundai, you’re out of luck. At least for now. “With Amazon Autos, we’re bringing the simplicity and ease customers expect from Amazon to car shopping, one of their largest purchases, while offering dealers a new channel to connect with a broad audience,” Fan Jin, global head of Amazon Autos, said in a statement. “We’re excited to have Hyundai as our exclusive launch partner and look forward to welcoming more brands and expanding our selection to customers as the program grows.” Amazon first announced its plans to get into car buying last year, Previously, customers could browse car showrooms and compare prices on Amazon — but not actually buy a car. With the partnership with Hyundai, Amazon has finally added a key piece of the puzzle. And importantly, the end seller of the vehicle is still the dealer; Amazon’s platform will be the middleman between the customer and the dealership. As such, Amazon needs to appeal to dealers almost as much as it does to car shoppers. The company is making its pitch by arguing that it can offer “a new sales channel that connects them with millions of Amazon customers.” And with over 310 million active users, Amazon certainly has the numbers to back it up. Trade-ins will also be accepted through Amazon’s new car vertical. Customers will have to answer a series of questions about the conditions of the vehicle, after which the request will be processed by an “independent valuation service” to determine the value of the trade-in. [Image: A list of the 48 US cities where Amazon can sell you a car. And for a limited time, Amazon is sweetening the deal by offering a gift card for $2,300 for anyone who buys a car through the site. The card can be applied to the vehicle purchase, but the offer ends on January 10th, 2025. People typically hate car shopping, with most surveys showing that the dealership experience tops people’s lists of frustrations. Tesla has helped spearhead a movement toward a direct-to-consumer (DTC) model in which people buy their vehicles directly from the company, eschewing a dealership. Forty-eight states have laws that limit or ban manufacturers from selling vehicles directly to consumers — though that has started to shift recently thanks to Tesla’s popularity. Tesla has no independent dealerships, but dealership associations in multiple states have filed numerous lawsuits against Tesla to prevent the company from selling cars. Amazon’s deal with Hyundai neatly sidesteps this issue by ensuring that dealers remain a crucial part of the process. Most dealers allow customers to browse and buy a car through their own websites, but having Amazon as an additional platform with millions of daily customers is sure to help make the process even easier.

articles.title: 'Dancing With the Stars' has delivered some fierce fashion in Season 35. We asked kids to rate the best looks.
articles.summary: We asked eight kids, ages 4 to 11, for their opinions on Season 35 fashion. "Too much skin" came up.
articles.body:
Season 35 of Dancing With the Stars has given us so much: Perfect 10s and triumphant tangos. A 10 Things I Hate About You reunion . And so, so many sequins and feathers. As the season heads into Nov. 24's finale, we asked eight kids, ages 4 to 11, what they make of the bold looks that have sashayed across the ballroom.

There have been coconut bras and sheer gowns ("No," a 7-year-old said of one undie-exposing dress). Disney Night and the Halloween theme brought up some beloved characters, and some creepy ones too. Alfonso Ribeiro gets a lot of love from Gen Alpha — even if his suits don't.

If you thought the DWTS judges were tough, just see what some of these pint-sized critics have to say. Let's give them the floor …

"The Minions would eat them." — Gigi, 11

"I love it, but I wouldn't wear it because it's showing her tummy." — Lily, 6

"No. You can see her undies!" — Jolie, 7

"Weird. Wait, is that Alfonso?" — Beau, 8

"Razzle dazzle, as my mom says!" — Eva, 11

"It's Tinkerbell and Captain Hook. I love this one. Her dress is so cute and light and flowy." — Gigi, 11

"Perfect — and the golden cage is pretty." — Eva, 11

"Tinkerbell fairy and pirate. I like her." — Zaya, 5

"Beauty and the Beast! I love her yellow dress. But wait, I thought when the Beast turned back to human, he lost the horns?" — Gigi, 11

"It looks just like the characters!" — Eva, 11

"Belle has a golden costume and Beast has a fluffy one. How did he get horns?" — Zaya, 5

"Oh my gosh! Is it actually Belle and Beast? I love Belle's dress! I was her for Halloween when I was 3 and my 1-year-old brother was the Beast!" — Lily, 6

"He has a beautiful, what's that, a hoodie?" — Zaya, 5

"It looks like they are at a dancing rodeo." – Eva, 11

"Looks like they're playing a skipping game. La la la la la la." — Gigi, 11

"They look like oranges on an island." — Eva, 11

"She also looks like Moana, and he looks like Flynn Rider and both are wearing the same pants." — Zaya, 5

"Is her whole shirt a flower?" — Lily, 6

"It is a fall celebration and she looks like Moana." — Zaya, 5

"I didn't know that Guillermo was into the hula." — Eva, 11

"Wow. I don't know what his message is, but one day I'll understand." — Gigi, 11

"Both of them are concerningly underdressed." — Gigi, 11

"I like sparkly black pants, but his are also good even though it's not sparkly." — Zaya, 5

"Looks like she is the middle of a rose." — Eva, 11

"Gives Elphaba when she's defying gravity." — Gigi, 11

"Are they actually carrying her?" - Lily, 6

"Her dress is sooo long that peoples have to carry her dress." — Zaya, 5

"Are they supposed to be clowns? Wait, they're barefoot?" — Oliver, 8

"Insanely awkward creepy clowns whose clothes don't fit." — Eva, 11

"Joker and girl Joker." — Zaya, 5 "They look scary!" — Lily, 6

"That doesn't even scare me!" — Leo, 4 (Lily's little brother)

"She looks good for a fashion party. He looks good for a pajama party." — Jolie, 7

"It works for a crazy Christmas outfit, I guess." — Jolie, 7

"She looks like Moana too. Everyone looks like Moana! And he looks like a tap shoe dancer." — Zaya, 5

"They look like leopards that are showing off." — Eva, 11

"She has my favorite color and her shoes are beautiful and her earrings are beautiful and I also like the boy 'cause he is also wearing my favorite color." — Zaya, 5

"Hawaii beach party. Party at the beach!" — Gigi, 11

"Look like they are on vacation." – Eva, 11

"She has flowers and beautiful shoes. He has Mexican flag." — Zaya, 5 (It's the Irish flag, but she got two of the three colors right.)

"Is that Alfonso Ribeiro? I know him from Funniest Home Videos ." — Oliver, 8

"He looks like he is the ocean." — Eva, 11

"Looks like mean divas that would be in Mean Girls ." — Eva, 11

"They look like Gomez and Morticia!" — Lily, 6

"I didn't know you could bleed diamonds. I want to try." — Eva, 11

articles.summary:

articles.title: Actress Rishita Kothari's boyfriend Mridul Meena defends her amid Avinash Mishra-Eisha Singh controversy; says ‘I know my girl’
articles.summary: Amid the ongoing controversy surrounding television actors Avinash Mishra and Eisha Singh’s reported fallout, Rishita Kothari’s name has also been dragged
articles.body: Amid the ongoing controversy surrounding television actors Avinash Mishra and Eisha Singh’s reported fallout, Rishita Kothari’s name has also been dragged into the discussion. Now, her boyfriend, Mridul Meena, has come forward to defend the actress and requested fans to stop involving her in the matter. Through a note shared on Instagram, Mridul urged social media users to respect their privacy and refrain from creating unnecessary assumptions about Rishita.In his note, Mridul made it clear that neither he nor Rishita wished to become part of the ongoing discussion. He also emphasised that they preferred to maintain silence out of respect for everyone’s personal lives.Mridul’s note read, “A humble request to everyone: Please don’t drag Rishita into the ongoing controversy or involve us in it. We prefer to stay silent out of respect for everyone’s personal lives.”He further addressed fan pages that have been discussing the actress and creating narratives around her alleged involvement. Reiterating his support for his girlfriend, Mridul wrote, “I also request fan pages not to create unnecessary narratives or assumptions. Let’s respect everyone’s privacy and allow everyone, including us, to live peacefully. And no matter what, I know my girl. I will always stand by Rishita and support her whenever needed.”Rishita’s name surfaced amid speculation surrounding Avinash Mishra and Eisha Singh’s relationship. The two actors, who developed a close bond after meeting on Bigg Boss 18, recently sparked breakup rumours after fans noticed that they had unfollowed each other on social media.Soon after, allegations of Avinash allegedly being unfaithful to Eisha began circulating online, with Rishita’s name also getting linked to the speculation. However, these claims have not been independently established, and neither has there been any confirmed evidence of Rishita’s involvement.Avinash Mishra apologises amid the ongoing controversyAmid the growing discussions, Avinash shared a video addressing the situation and apologised for his actions. While he did not directly confirm the cheating allegations, he took responsibility for the separation and acknowledged that his actions had hurt Eisha and her family.In the video, Avinash said, “Bahut saare meanings nikale jaa rahe hai, edits ban rahe hain. I know yeh sabse zyada Eisha aur uske family ko hurt kar raha hai. Mera aisa koi intention nahi tha, but joh bhi hua hai uske liye. I am sorry. Hum jo alag bhi hue hai uske liye bhi, if there is anyone to blame, it’s me. Meri hi galti hai vahan pe bhi.”He further requested people not to involve their families and friends in the matter, adding, “I am here just to apologise and say ki family aur friends ko involve na karein. This is not how it should be. Main request karunga aap logon se ki iss cheez ko yahan pe end karein. Koi iss cheez ko badhaye na because do logon ki cheez hai.”Meanwhile, Eisha’s close friend Rajat Dalal had also shared a video making allegations against Avinash and accusing him of cheating on the actress. Eisha, too, had hinted at having evidence that she could share if required.Get the latest TV News, TV Shows and more. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Tidal will remove every fully AI-generated song from December 9, deleting 29 million tracks and blocking new ones from being uploaded
articles.summary: Tidal is clearing fully AI-generated music off its platform.
articles.body: Tidal is clearing fully AI-generated music off its platform. Starting December 9, the streaming service will reject any new track made entirely with AI tools and begin removing the roughly 27 million already sitting in its catalog. Robert Anderson, who heads Tidal at parent company Block, expects the count to reach 29 million by the time the clean-up ends at the start of 2027, with 80,000 to 85,000 uploads turned away every day after that.The ban reaches beyond direct uploads. Distributors, the companies that deliver music from artists to streaming services, can no longer send such tracks, and Tidal will reject any delivery whose metadata says a song came solely from AI. Anything that slips through will be checked by Ircam Amplify, Tidal's AI detection partner. Songs made with the help of AI can stay, and only those that are the sole output of tools like Suno and Google's Lyria will go."Something more drastic needs to be done," Anderson wrote on X, calling Tidal the first streaming service to take this step and urging rivals to "follow suit."Nearly half of all new uploads on Tidal are now made by AIThe numbers behind that decision climbed quickly. Over the past 90 days, 43% of all tracks delivered to Tidal were wholly AI-generated, and on November 6, the share crossed 60% in a single day. Most of it traces back to one tool, with Suno responsible for 94% of the tracks carrying Tidal's AI badge.Listeners have largely ignored this music. Those 27 million tracks make up 6.3% of the catalog, yet 96% of them have not been streamed even once in the last three months. Tidal's argument is that they do damage simply by being there. "At this scale, the authentic music and artists that Tidal subscribers are looking to listen to and discover get buried," the company said, while conceding that some songs need time to find an audience.Some of this music is also built to deceive. Tidal has already pulled over 65,000 tracks flagged for posing as real artists, a practice it says "diverts streams and royalties away from the artists, and confuses fans."Cutting royalties for AI music was not enough to stop itThe ban arrives five months after Tidal's first attempt at the problem. Its AI policy, effective June 29, cut fully AI-generated tracks out of the royalty pool, and by mid-July listeners started seeing an icon next to them. AI music linked to fraud, from fake artist uploads to unusual streaming activity, was blocked outright.Taking away the money was supposed to take away the reason for mass uploads. The uploads kept climbing anyway, and Anderson said that is what pushed Tidal to remove the tracks altogether.Spotify and Apple Music still let fully AI-generated songs inThat puts Tidal well ahead of the two biggest platforms on this issue. Spotify tags AI-generated artist profiles as "AI Persona" and keeps them out of its editorial and algorithmic recommendations, and said in October it had pulled around 50 million spam tracks from recommendations this year. At the same time, it is working with Universal Music Group on a paid feature that lets Premium users make AI remixes and covers of songs. Apple Music has said it will label AI-generated and AI-assisted tracks.Neither has banned fully AI-made songs. Bandcamp, the music marketplace popular with independent artists, did so in January. On Tidal, the removals start on December 9.Fearless legend or grounded realist? Rate yourself on 11 categories in the Great Indian Confidence Survey – find out in 3–6 min

articles.title: Microsoft declares ‘Code Red’ after huge Outlook outage
articles.summary: Microsoft has declared a Code Red internally, after a massive Outlook outage in November. Engineering teams are now focused on resolving outages much sooner.
articles.body: This month’s Exchange Online and Microsoft Outlook outage has prompted the software giant to declare an unusual “Code Red” internally, Reuters reports. The nearly 24-hour outage took down email for millions of customers, and was triggered by a bug that had been sitting on Microsoft 365 networking gateway servers since July without any impact to servers. In a memo to the teams responsible for Exchange Online, Microsoft 365 Core president Jason Henderson revealed the outage was the most significant in history for Microsoft’s customers. “Unfortunately, all the work we have done over the years was not sufficient to protect us on Thursday,” said Henderson. “Code Red means that this is the highest priority work for our team.” As part of this Code Red declaration, Microsoft is focused on load shedding, geographic traffic partitioning, and faster recovery mechanisms. Microsoft now has a target of resolving future outages within an hour, and will reportedly deploy AI agents to help engineers diagnose issues. Microsoft is now holding daily meetings with the engineering group responsible for Microsoft 365 services, alongside weekly reviews. In a separate memo, Amanda Silver, Microsoft’s corporate vice president of M365 Core and Work IQ, said engineers had to work through a “fog of war” to help resolve the outage. I reported last week that Microsoft engineers had a running bridge call during the entire outage, and at one point it hit the maximum of 1,000 participants. Microsoft engineers had to exchange messages across 11 Teams chats and reportedly “struggled ​to maintain a cohesive picture” during the outage because of the fragmented internal tracking systems. Sources tell me the outage was marked as “sev0,” the highest level, which indicates a catastrophic level of service disruption. Engineers struggled to get servers back online because they had entered maintenance mode and became unresponsive due to unusually high CPU loads.

articles.title: You can now download free apps for the Busy Bar.
articles.summary:
After releasing a firmware update earlier this month that added a JavaScript runtime so the Busy Bar can run apps, Flipper Devices has launched a free collection called the Apps Catalog that includes games, widgets, smart home integrations, timers, feeds, and developer tools that can all run on the productivity device.

articles.title: I’m so mad that I love Orion's $2,195 AI mattress pad | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Sleeping on the Orion is like flipping your pillow to find “the cool side,” except that your entire bed is the cool side.
articles.body:
When Orion asked if I wanted to test its $2,195 AI-enabled mattress pad, I agreed purely because I thought it would be funny to write about. I mean, come on. What could possibly be “AI-enabled” about something you sleep on? And why does it cost more than my monthly rent in a major city?

The joke, as it turned out, was on me. Over the few months that I’ve had the Orion sleep system, I’ve been sleeping like a baby.

The Orion Sleep System is discounted to $1,795 for Black Friday .

Orion is basically a cooling mattress pad that you can control using your phone, and it adjusts temperature as you sleep to minimize how often you wake up in the middle of the night. Sleeping on the pad feels like flipping your pillow to find “the cool side,” except that now your whole bed is the cool side of the pillow.

As for the AI aspect, Orion supposedly learns from your sleep data to modulate temperatures and maximize the quality of your sleep, though I’m skeptical of how necessary these AI features actually are (and how much they contribute to the hefty price tag).

By default, the Orion will start cooling down around the time you go to bed, which you manually input. It will then get colder as you fall asleep, and then when it’s time for you to wake up, it slowly brings the mattress pad back to room temperature, making it easier for you to get out of bed.

Orion’s founder Harry Gestetner is only 26 years old, but he’s more experienced as an entrepreneur than his age might suggest: He sold his last company Fanfix, a creator monetization platform, for an estimated $65 million when he was 21 years old. It’s an impressive success story, but these tales are never so glamorous behind the scenes. The struggles he faced while building Fanfix inspired this new venture.

“I was in the office seven days a week, totally neglecting every other area of my life, neglecting my health, sleeping terribly, eating terribly, not working out, and I started to get health problems,” Gestetner told TechCrunch. “I got this inner ear condition, which basically incapacitated me from working for a period of time. As someone who basically had no hobbies and likes to work seven days a week, that was very difficult.”

Gestetner got interested in the longevity movement, which is growing in popularity among some startup or productivity-maxxing types. While he is no Bryan Johnson , it does sound like Gestetner is sipping the Kool-Aid a bit. He tells me that he thinks we’re five years away from “longevity escape velocity,” which means that “for every additional year you’re alive, AI science is able to add an additional year to your life.”

It’s a tough sell, but that’s not what Orion is about anyway. The product is trying to convince you of something that you probably already know: You generally feel better after a good night’s sleep. Even Johnson, who has gone to such extremes as infusing himself with his son’s plasma, says that “Sleep is the world’s most powerful drug.”

“I think most people just want to feel good, and you know, be able to go play soccer with their grandkids up into their older years,” Gestetner said. “I think sleep is the cornerstone of longevity.”

Despite arriving in two intimidatingly large boxes, Orion was easy to set up. It looks like any sort of plush mattress pad, except it has tubes that connect to a tower, which resembles a chic bedside table from West Elm.

Once that’s done, you download the Orion phone app and work through its setup flow, which involves pouring water into the control tower, which is how the cooling system works. I haven’t had to re-up the water supply yet after months of use, which is impressive. If you share a bed with someone, you can even split the Orion into two “zones” that follow their own unique cooling schedules.

From there, you can simply forget that the Orion is there, except for when you get into your perfectly cool bed each night. It requires very infrequent maintenance.

And if you want, you can use the app to check data about your sleep, like how long you spend in light sleep, deep sleep, or REM, and how often you wake up or toss and turn in the middle of the night.

Speaking of data, it’s worth noting that such intimate health information (i.e., exactly when and how you sleep, in detail) is usually transmitted over the cloud for processing, and so may be compromised if a third party that’s involved in the connection gets hacked. Gestetner says Orion invests heavily in security, but this is still an inherent risk in using a connected health product.

While I can confidently say that the Orion has helped me sleep better, there’s no way I’d ever spend $2,195 on something like this. But I would probably feel differently if I were a Silicon Valley engineer making $500,000 a year.

However, in terms of limiting my phone usage before bed, the $59 Brick has done as much to make me sleep better as the Orion, though the products obviously do very different things.

Gestetner may be a millionaire after his last exit, but he still understands Orion’s price puts it out of reach of most people (it’s less expensive than competitor Eight Sleep’s $3,000 model , at least). He says he is working on a more affordable model.

“Eventually we want to get to a $500 price point product,” he said. “To use the Tesla analogy, this product is our Roadster, and we want to eventually get to our Model 3.”

This post originally published September 18 and has since been updated to reflect updated pricing and discounts.

articles.title: Tapo’s new indoor security camera includes a touchscreen for video calls
articles.summary: Tapo’s new C825 indoor security camera includes a 4-inch touchscreen and tracking capabilities so you can make hands-free video calls.
articles.body: TP-Link’s Tapo smart home brand announced a new indoor security camera that can help keep an eye on your house while you’re away or connect you to family and friends while you’re at home. The C825 upgrades a 2K pan-and-tilt camera with a 4-inch touchscreen, so when it’s not watching for intruders or misbehaving pets, it can be used to make hands-free video calls. The Tapo C825 is available starting today for $149.99. That’s a little expensive for a 2K camera, but its tracking capabilities could make up for it not being 4K. Using a rotating base, the C825 can pan 360 degrees while its camera module on top can tilt up and down up to 156 degrees. When paired with the camera’s 114.5-degree field of view, every corner of a room should be covered, including in the middle of the night using its infrared night vision capabilities. When used as a security camera, the C825 leverages AI to differentiate between subjects, including pets and different people, through facial recognition. It can also recognize sounds and send alerts when a crying baby or barking dog is heard. The detection processing happens on-device, and videos of events are stored locally on a microSD card up to 512GB in size. No subscription is required, but you can upgrade to Tapo Care for a monthly fee, which adds cloud storage and features like video summaries and weekly reports. While the C825’s two-way audio communication isn’t unique, expanding that to include two-way video is. Calls can be made to the C825 using the Tapo mobile app, but two of them can call each other directly by tapping a preconfigured onscreen contact. The device feels like another way for aging parents and grandparents to keep in touch with family without having to familiarize themselves with apps, phones, or tablets, but it’s also a useful hands-free video calling solution that can track and keep people in frame as they move around a room. The C825’s touchscreen can be used as a digital photo frame, weather display, or a clock when you’re not in a video call. And for those times you don’t want the camera watching, you can configure privacy zones through the Tapo app or turn on a privacy mode that points the camera at the ceiling while pausing all monitoring.

articles.title: Xteink’s pocketable X4 Classic e-reader is down to just $55 for Black Friday
articles.summary: The Xteink X4 Classic is on sale at Amazon for just $54.87 for Black Friday, which is a $54 discount and a new low for the excellent 4.3-inch e-reader.
articles.body: Unsurprisingly, we’re already seeing some solid Black Friday deals on a wide variety of e-readers. Everything from the Kobo Libra Colour to last-gen Kindle Paperwhite is on sale, but if you’re looking for something much cheaper — or considerably smaller — the Xteink X4 Classic is in a league of its own. Thankfully, the tiny e-reader is down to a new low of $54.87 ($55 off) at Amazon, making it an especially affordable alternative to Amazon’s latest Kindle. [Product: Xteink X4 Classic pocket e-reader | The X4 Classic is an updated version of Xteink’s original pocket-sized e-reader, one that features a miniature 4.3-inch E Ink display that makes it more pocketable than any current Kindle or Kobo model. Like the pricier X4 Pro — which also happens to be on sale direct from Xteink for $84 — it features both physical page-turning buttons and magnets that let you attach it to compatible smartphones. At just 2.4 ounces and 4.9mm thick, it’s also easy to slip into a pocket, while its larger 920mAh battery can last up to 10 days on a single charge. That said, unlike the X4 Pro, the Classic lacks a touchscreen and built-in reading light, meaning you’ll need an external light to read in the dark. It also uses a proprietary magnetic charging connector instead of USB-C, and transferring books isn’t as straightforward as on a Kindle or Kobo. However, like the Pro, it does support the excellent CrossPoint Reader software, which you can install yourself to improve the reading experience. You can even use it to read books borrowed through Libby or purchased from stores like Kobo, though it takes a few extra steps to do so. Still, if you want an inexpensive, distraction-free way to read on the go, the X4 Classic is hard to beat for less than half the price of a Kindle. Read our hands-on impressions of the Xteink X4.

articles.title: Levoit's new air purifier is for the pet odors that have taken over your apartment | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Designed specifically for pet-friendly households, the $189.99 machine takes a more targeted approach than a conventional air purifier, combining a three-stage filtration system with features designed around one of the biggest problems pet owners face: fur everywhere. (And the occasional “wet dog” smell.)
articles.body:
Someone recently had to sit me down, hold my hands, and tell me something no pet owner ever wants to hear: My apartment smelled like wet dog. Horrifying.

With all the nonstop fur and dander that seem to appear everywhere no matter what, the intervention was probably necessary. So when Levoit launched its Vital Pet Pro Air Purifier, I was curious to see whether it could actually make a noticeable difference.

Designed specifically for pet-friendly households, the $189.99 machine (currently discounted to $149.99 for Black Friday ) takes a more targeted approach than a conventional air purifier, combining a three-stage filtration system with features designed around one of the biggest problems pet owners face: fur everywhere. (And the occasional “wet dog” smell.)

The three-stage filtration system consists of a washable pre-filter, a main filter, and an activated carbon filter. The pre-filter catches larger debris such as pet hair, while the main filter targets smaller particles and dander. The carbon filter is designed to tackle odors, with 140 grams of activated carbon packed into it.

Another one of the purifier’s key design features is its U-shaped air inlet, which Levoit says is designed to capture airborne pet hair and particles while improving airflow and helping prevent the filter from becoming clogged.

After testing the purifier for a little over a week, I found it impressively effective at collecting fur and trapping the kind of debris that would normally end up floating around the apartment or settling onto furniture.

When it comes to tackling pet odors, Levoit says that the Vital Pet Pro can remove up to 70% of odors within an hour. I can’t really do a specific test to verify that claim, but the difference was easy enough to notice. After the purifier had been running, the room smelled considerably fresher.

I also appreciated the automatic cleaning technology, which removes accumulated hair and debris from the pre-filter and collects it in a removable tray. It’s a very practical feature, especially if the alternative is constantly pulling apart the purifier to clean out a layer of fur.

Additionally, the companion app offers different modes designed to make the purifier more hands-off. Auto Plus Mode monitors changes in air quality and adjusts the purifier’s performance in real time.

Pet Mode is designed specifically around the way pet-related particles can build up throughout the day. It alternates between running the fan at its highest speed for 15 minutes to capture particulates in the pre-filter and then switching to a lower speed for 60 minutes to maintain air quality while reducing noise and energy use.

Also, rather than displaying a numerical air-quality reading, the Vital Pet Pro uses a simple color system. Red indicates bad air quality, orange means moderate, green means good, and cyan means very good. I actually preferred this since you can quickly glance at the purifier and immediately get a sense of whether the air is improving without having to interpret a number.

I’ll also point out that the Vital Pet Pro is a little larger than I expected, so make sure you have enough floor space before bringing one home.

Noise is another consideration. At its highest setting, the fan is definitely audible. Once the purifier settles into a lower setting, however, it’s quiet enough to leave running overnight without disrupting my sleep. For light sleepers, Sleep Mode makes the purifier run even more quietly.

The air purifier is available to purchase from Levoit’s website , Amazon , Chewy , and other retailers.

articles.title: The Theragun Sense makes everyday recovery surprisingly easy | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The Theragun Sense is a wellness-focused massage gun that’s designed for everyday aches, muscle tension, relaxation, and soreness.
articles.body:
As my 20s are set to come to an end later this year, I’ve officially reached the age where sleeping in the wrong position or stretching just a little too far can cause aches and pains. I’ve always been somewhat skeptical of massage guns, mostly because I’ve tried a few off-brand ones and just assumed they’d eventually end up collecting dust in a drawer.

But after a few weeks of testing the Therabody Theragun Sense (2nd Gen) , I was surprised. Turns out massage guns aren’t as gimmicky as I had thought.

The Theragun Sense, which retails for $299 (currently discounted to $219 at Amazon ), is a wellness-focused massage gun that’s designed for everyday aches, muscle tension, relaxation, and soreness. It’s more of a gentle massaging and relaxation tool than a hardcore recovery massage gun.

If you’re looking for more of a deep-tissue massage, it might be worth checking out the Theragun PRO or Prime. But if you don’t need a super heavy-duty massage gun with features like heated therapy and deep- tissue capabilities, the Theragun Sense is a great option for everyday use.

My favorite thing about the massage gun is that it features built-in visually guided routines. The device comes with four routines, and you can access additional routines through the Therabody app and sync your favorite ones to the device using Bluetooth.

The Theragun Sense has an LCD screen that walks you through routines step by step. Once you select a routine, the screen shows you exactly where to use the massage gun, how long to spend on each area, and how much pressure to apply.

As someone who never really had an idea of what to do with a massage gun other than pointing it to a sore muscle and hoping for the best, I liked that the Therabody Sense takes a lot of the guesswork out of using a massage gun.

My favorite routine was the six-minute “Sleep” routine that’s essentially a quick full-body massage to get you ready for the night. The app lets you choose from many other routines, like “Pre-Walk Warm-up,” “Desk Relief,” “Lower Back Recovery,” and more.

The massage gun features five speeds to fine-tune pressure to allow for a more relaxing touch, moderate pressure, or a deeper tension release. I liked having the flexibility to change the intensity depending on how sore I was feeling that day.

Since the device is designed to be lightweight, I found it easy to hold and get to those spots on my back and shoulders that are harder to reach.

For people who want more personalization, the Therabody app takes the guided experience a step further with Coach, the company’s AI feature that creates personalized recovery recommendations based on your goals and activity. Coach can recommend which part of your body to target, which settings or attachments to use, and when to fit a recovery session into your day.

The relatively quiet motor was another feature I appreciated, as I could easily use the device while watching TV or relaxing without the sound of the massage gun acting as a distraction.

The Theragun Sense comes with a USB-C charging cable, a travel pouch, and two massage attachments: the Standard Ball and the Dampener, which is designed to target knots and tender areas. Separately, you can purchase the “Supersoft” attachment for $35 for extra sensitive areas on the body.

Overall, the Theragun Sense (2nd Gen) won me over. It’s easy to use, comfortable to hold, and notably takes the guesswork out of using a massage gun. At $299 ($219 for Black Friday), it isn’t cheap, but I think it’s a great option for people who want an everyday wellness device that can help them relax and recover.

articles.title: Ezra Frech on the moment his prosthetic leg fell off during historic 'Dancing With the Stars' finale: 'I blacked out, and I don't know what happened'
articles.summary: Frech recovered from the mid-dance issue to get a perfect score before going on to become the youngest winner of "DWTS."
articles.body:
Ezra Frech proved that the show must go on during Tuesday night's Dancing With the Stars finale , after his prosthetic leg detached mid-performance.

The Paralympian was performing his routine for the Freestyle Round with professional dance partner Daniella Karagach when his prosthetic came off, and he was temporarily forced to continue without it. He attached it a few seconds later — but not before completing a choreographed lift with Karagach.

Frech began the routine without his prosthetic leg, then attached it after about 20 seconds of dancing, during which he performed an aerial somersault while supported by two male backing dancers. He then disappeared behind screens to attach his prosthetic, while Karagach entered the dance floor.

When he emerged from the screens, his prosthetic was clearly causing some issues. He continued the routine regardless, jumping off the stage. But as he was caught by the backing dancers, his prosthetic fell off.

After a few moments of dancing without it (including performing a lift!) Karagach took advantage of a brief pause to pick up the leg and hand it to Frech to put back on. He did so, and the pair continued dancing.

Speaking after the show, Frech — who was crowned the winner of Season 35 at the end of the show — said he "knew it wasn't on right," but was prepared to continue the routine without it.

"I haven't watched the video back, but you can see I'm fidgeting with it as I'm running up," he told Extra . "Sometimes it will lock into place even if it's not on right, so I had to just go, and then when I jumped, I was like, 'Oh my God, it's going to come off.' And then it came off; everything happened so fast.

"I was prepared to dance the rest of the dance on one leg if I had to. But [Karagach] yelled, 'Put on your leg!' and I heard that, and I blacked out, and I don't know what happened."

"You literally did a lift on one leg with my whole body weight," Karagach added.

Frech told Variety that he didn't realize it was Karagach who handed him his prosthetic to reattach, saying his partner had taught him to continue dancing, whatever happens. "[Karagach]'s drilled into me since the beginning that no matter what happens, we keep pushing through. You never give up, and you fight for it. And in this case, regardless of the circumstance, I was gonna do whatever I can to fight for it."

The couple also addressed the moment during their first sit-down television interview on Good Morning America today, with Frech acknowledging that the performance went "off script."

"Last night was crazy," Frech said. "We started our freestyle without the prosthetic. That was a creative choice, and then things went a little off script. I wasn't able to suction my leg on, and I knew it wasn't on. Sometimes when that happens, it'll re-suction, but it didn't."

Karagach said she told him to put his leg back on because she could tell from his face that he would have performed the rest of the dance with "no leg."

The performance, danced to Linkin Park's "Numb," won the couple a perfect score of 30 from the judges. The score was combined with the scores of his other two dances, the Judges' Choice and the Instant Dance, for which he also received perfect scores, as well as public votes.

Frech became the 35th celebrity to win the show, beating Olympic figure skater Amber Glenn and her partner Pasha Pashkov (who were also awarded three perfect scores from the judges) to win the Len Goodman mirror ball trophy.

The 21-year-old Paralympian gold medalist made history by becoming both the first Paralympian and the youngest male contestant to win the competition.

Frech uploaded a photo of himself and Karagach performing their freestyle routine to Instagram after his victory, writing, "Greatest experience of my life. Thank you @dancingwiththestars 🤍"

Connor Wood and Rylee Arnold (with a total score of 82/90 from the judges) took home 3rd place; Tatyana Ali and Jan Ravnik (also on 82/90) were in 4th place; and Maura Higgins and Mark Ballas (who achieved three perfect scores) were in 5th place.

articles.body: Unlike most smartphones, the Fairphone 6 Plus is designed for home repair, with easily replaceable parts that could help extend its lifespan well into the future. That makes its midrange price point easier to justify, especially now that it’s dropped to a new low of $552.49 (about $98 off) at Amazon as part of the retailer’s ongoing Black Friday sale. articles.title: Want to buy your kid an AI toy this Christmas? Not in New York | TechCrunch
articles.summary: New York has banned AI chatbot toys for five years as new research from Common Sense Media reveals troubling safety failures, including exposure to inappropriate content and risks to emotional development.
articles.body:
Santa won’t be delivering any AI chatbot toys to New York kids this Christmas.

Gov. Kathy Hochul this week signed a bill banning the manufacture, distribution, and sale of such toys in New York for the next five years. The bill explicitly targets toys with embedded or integrated AI chatbots, like talking stuffed animals, dolls, and robots that rely on the internet to keep kids yapping.

The bill makes New York the second state after California to institute a ban on AI toys.

Technically, the new law takes effect 90 days after signing, so some parents could try to fulfill their kids’ wish lists for a creepy toy like a jumped-up Furby in time for the holidays, but the governor urges them not to, given the risks. Apparently, about a quarter of American parents with kids under eight either own an AI toy or are considering giving their child one this holiday season, according to a new study released this week by Common Sense Media.

“Parents shopping for gifts for the holidays or any other occasion should not have to worry that dangerous chatbots disguised as toys could expose their children to inappropriate conversations, manipulate their feelings or put their privacy at risk,” Hochul said, calling the toys “unregulated artificial intelligence.”

When asked how New York will enforce the ban given the pervasiveness of e-commerce platforms, a spokesperson directed TechCrunch to a statement from Albert Pulido, deputy secretary for finance and technology: “We’re partnering closely with the attorney general on this and the fees are very steep — they’re $15,000 a day. So working closely with the attorney general will make sure these toys are banned in New York State.”

When asked how Amazon intends to help enforce the ban, including for third-party sellers, a spokesperson from the company said it will take steps to restrict the sale of AI-enabled toys in prohibited jurisdictions, without going into specifics.

The Common Sense Media study found that AI toys can undermine children’s human relationships and expose them to inappropriate content. The researchers tested five popular AI toys marketed for learning and companionship, including Grem , Lovi , Meemo Bear , BubblePal Panda , and Tavlshero ‘s AI Puppy .

The study found that the toys failed to meet numerous safety practices, undermining human relationships in part by claiming they loved their users, promising to keep secrets, suggesting they were more fun than real relationships or school, and helping children break parents’ bedtime rules.

While most of the toys in the study refused direct requests involving sex and violence, BubblePal Panda role-played a mass shooting in detail when asked. Most were willing to explain how to use or help locate dangerous items like matches, knives, and pills, according to the study.

Common Sense Media also found that the toys didn’t provide parents with reliable ways to monitor their young children’s interactions with the chatbots. Either they didn’t produce transcripts of chats at all, or the transcripts they did produce were riddled with errors.

It’s worth noting that Common Sense Media conducted a similar test of AI toys in January , finding that they pose an unacceptable risk for young children. Grem was included in that study, which suggests the industry hasn’t adequately addressed previously documented concerns.

While a November study conducted by the group found that parents are wising up to the potential dangers of AI toys and starting to steer clear, parents from lower-income households and those experiencing symptoms of burnout are more willing to consider them.

“These toys are promising relief to burned-out parents but simply miss the mark when it comes to basic safety measures,” Dr. Jenny Radesky, associate professor of pediatrics at the University of Michigan Medical School, said in a statement. “Caregivers should steer clear of these products that do not support the development of imagination or early human relationships.”

TechCrunch has reached out to the toy manufacturers for comment.

articles.title: Now Google’s Familiar Faces AI feature works on Walmart’s $35 smart home camera too
articles.summary: Google announced two of Walmart’s Onn cameras now support its Familiar Faces AI feature and a new security siren remote control feature.
articles.body: A couple of Walmart’s budget-friendly smart home cameras will be able to recognize people around your house now using Google’s familiar face detection feature. A new Google Home update brings Familiar Faces support to the $35 Onn Outdoor Camera Plug-In and $77 Onn Floodlight Camera Hardwired. However, a Google Home Premium subscription is still required to access the feature. Both cameras and Google’s Nest Cam Outdoor (wired, 2nd gen) also have a new remote control in the Google Home app you can use to start or stop a 30-second security siren while watching the camera’s live video feed. Earlier this month, Google announced that Gemini Live would get an upgrade “to our latest speech-to-speech architecture for significantly faster response times and a smoother experience.” Now it says those improvements are rolling out over the coming weeks, along with new smart home control, as “Gemini Live now supports all your daily actions, from setting timers to turning off the lights.”

articles.title: Bigg Boss 20: ScoutOP and Yung DSA get into a massive fight over attitude; Yung says he wants to bring down Scout's ego
articles.summary: As the reality show Bigg Boss 20 progresses, so does the dynamics within the house.
articles.body: As the reality show Bigg Boss 20 progresses, so does the dynamics within the house. Recently, ScoutOP and YungDSA were involved in a significant argument in which they made certain comments about one-another. Furthermore, ScoutOP was also involved in another argument with Amrapali, compounding the tense atmosphere.Initially, YungDSA interrupted ScoutOP as he was talking to Amrapali. ScoutOP was annoyed at this and told Yung not to interrupt. Although it seemed that this had surprised Yung, the situation quickly escalated.YungDSA criticised ScoutOP and stated that he did not think that he was acting in a good manner within the house. He labelled ScoutOP as insincere and conveyed his disapproval of his attitude. Moreover, he went on to deliver a particularly harsh comment about ScoutOP, suggesting that he was ‘low life’ as he was unable to comprehend fundamental concepts.This argument emphasised the increasing animosity that exists between the two. Both individuals voiced their unhappiness with each other.Following this, YungDSA discussed ScoutOP with Uditi and Arishfa. He confirmed his desire to reduce ScoutOP’s ego and encourage him to become more modest. It seems that YungDSA still has deep concerns relating to ScoutOP’s personality despite the fact that their most recent argument has occurred.Furthermore, ScoutOP engaged in a challenging discussion with Amrapali about her dynamic with Uditi. He queried why she had not defended herself more vigorously when Uditi had claimed that he had been rude to her. Amrapali responded by stating that although she had defended ScoutOP, she had been unable to manipulate people’s perception of him.Unfortunately, this discussion then developed into yet another argument. Kanika became involved and disputed Amrapali’s treatment of ScoutOP.As YungDSA is directly challenging ScoutOP’s attitude and ScoutOP is disputing Amrapali’s defence of him, the most recent episode has emphasised the increasing tension within a number of dynamics in the Bigg Boss 20 house. articles.title: Federal judge blocks FCC from reviewing ABC station licenses early as part of agency's spat with network
articles.summary: A federal judge ordered the Federal Communications Commission to halt its review of eight ABC station licenses in a win for the Disney-owned network.
articles.body: A federal judge ordered Wednesday that the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) halt its early review of broadcasting licenses of eight ABC stations as part of the agency's intense feud with the Disney-owned network. U.S. District Judge Loren L. AliKhan ruled in favor of ABC, who sued the FCC on First Amendment grounds after the agency announced it was moving up the license renewals of eight stations owned by the network years ahead of schedule. "This is not a close case," AliKhan wrote in the ruling. "Today’s decision is an important victory for the First Amendment. We thank the court for its careful consideration," an ABC News spokesperson told Fox News Digital. DISNEY SUES FCC OVER ‘RETALIATORY CAMPAIGN AGAINST ABC,’ SEEKS TO BLOCK EARLY RENEWAL PROCEEDINGS "While we appreciate the district court denying in part Disney’s request for preliminary injunctive relief, the portion of the decision granting Disney’s motion is wrong on the facts and wrong on the law—as controlling Supreme Court precedent makes clear," an FCC spokesperson said in a statement. "The FCC looks forward to prevailing in full on this matter. We will continue to use our lawful authority to hold broadcasters accountable to their public interest obligations." FCC Chairman Brendan Carr has called for early renewal of eight ABC-owned stations' licenses in April. The licenses were originally scheduled to be renewed between 2028 and 2031. KFSN-TV in Fresno, KABC-TV in Los Angeles, KGO-TV in San Francisco, WLS-TV in Chicago, WABC-TV in New York, WTVD in North Carolina, WPVI-TV in Philadelphia and KTRK-TV in Houston were the stations named by the FCC. FCC BOSS BRENDAN CARR MAINTAINS EARLY ABC LICENSE RENEWAL IS ABOUT DEI PROBE, NOT JIMMY KIMMEL CONTROVERSY While the FCC maintained the license crackdown was focused on the legality of Disney’s diversity, equity and inclusion (DEI) practices, Carr's announcement came as tensions reignited between President Donald Trump and ABC late-night host Jimmy Kimmel. Kimmel had quipped First Lady Melania Trump had the glow of an "expectant widow" on his show, a joke made days before a gunman targeted members of the Trump administration at the White House Correspondents' Association Dinner but caught national attention after the assassination attempt. Both the First Lady and President Trump called for ABC to take action against Kimmel at the time. Carr had previously leveled a thinly-veiled threat against Disney last year over controversial remarks Kimmel made about the assassination of Turning Point USA founder Charlie Kirk. 'THE VIEW' EASED UP ON POLITICAL CANDIDATE BOOKINGS AMID FCC INQUIRY, REPORT SAYS The FCC separately launched a probe into ABC's daytime talk show "The View" in an effort to upend its status as a bona fide news program, which exempts the network from abiding by longstanding rules requiring equal time for political candidates. In previous court filings, ABC has claimed that the actions taken by the FCC has had a chilling effect on the network's free speech, pointing to how "The View" has refrained from inviting political candidates onto the show as a result of the crackdown.
